premises.text: Mobile fragmentation increases development costs for app developers.
premises.evidence_span: mobile fragmentation is now really ruining for mobile app developers. Irrespective of the size of the team, you're now probably spending one-third of your total development budget just on testing.

premises.text: Existing solutions require developers to write unit tests, which are often disliked.
premises.evidence_span: they ask developers to write unit tests. And not many developers actually like doing that.

premises.text: Accessing real physical devices remotely can improve testing and debugging.
premises.evidence_span: we put all of those devices into one tablet, so you can access those devices and interact with them as if they were on your desk.

premises.text: Real-time interaction with devices can enhance the debugging process.
premises.evidence_span: you can interact and then... you can slowly debug it step by step because you can see what happens in the source code.

premises.text: Developers can test on one device and replicate touch events across multiple devices.
premises.evidence_span: if you want to, you can test on one device and all of those touch events will be replicated on all of the devices in the cloud.

premises.text: The technology can support a large number of devices with fewer data centers.
premises.evidence_span: one server can support up to 250 devices. We started off with seven.

premises.text: The market for app testing and debugging is significant and growing.
premises.evidence_span: that makes it a $10 billion market. And those numbers are only going to go up.

value.text: Developers can access and interact with any mobile device efficiently and cost-effectively.
value.evidence_span: you save money. You can access any device anytime you want for a fraction of cost.

notes: No separate premises for features like algorithms and rack shells as they support the main technology premise.
